sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 39 (check 38), Internal Quality Checks row 39 (check 38, no extra annotation beyond the definition), Deterministic Checks row 5 (check-batched-independence-wording.py)
evidence: All three scored dimensions carry explicit independence-and-continue wording; no scored prompt or criterion tells the judge to stop at the first failure. functional/prompt.md:57-59 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion.'; also :9 'that criterion fails and scores 0; report what you saw and move on to the next criterion', :24 'Never carry a verdict across criteria', :29 'Two failed attempts at the same control fail that criterion; continue.' Functional additionally runs mode = "individual" (functional/judge.toml line 6), so each of the 16 criteria is graded in its own session (prompt :76 'Each session grades one criterion'), structurally preventing one miss from zeroing the rest. polish/prompt.md:20-26 '## Independent scoring ... One failed criterion does not zero the others. If a criterion cannot be performed, mark it failed and continue to every remaining criterion; return a verdict for all of them.' (polish mode = batched). visual/prompt.md:38-43 same block, with 'mark it with its 0 anchor and continue' (visual mode = batched). The only all-or-nothing rule is the template-standard in-dimension global browser gate (identical clause present in the template prompts), which the prompts explicitly name as the sole exception; gates/render and gates/constraints are all_pass and exempt per workbook Deterministic Checks row 5. Grep of scored judge.toml criterion text for stop/abort/earlier/remaining/depend found no cross-criterion zeroing directive (functional/judge.toml:226 'normal sending stops working' is a product behaviour, not a judge instruction). Adversarial: a broken app that fails signin_and_client_scope still has every later functional criterion graded in separate sessions as long as gwen can sign in (global gate); a conforming app that fails one polish behaviour (e.g. escape_closes) cannot lose enter_sends etc. under the wording. Per-criterion conjunctive legs within one criterion are allowed bundling (SKILL known false positives). Manual application of check-batched-independence-wording.py behaviour; the private checker executable was not run, and no configured judge run on these bytes exists (raw-evidence-index scope), so judge compliance with the wording is not observed - but this row is a prompt-wording check and that runtime gap belongs to the workload/judge-run rows.
